title: 第5章：桥上救人，绝地撤退
slug: 丧尸爆发我的房车能无限升级
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

“桥那边——那是什么东西？！”

眼镜男的嗓子快劈了，声带挤出来的频率能划玻璃。

林昊没空理他。

面板上红色倒计时在跳——【07:42】。

他扫了一眼大巴内部。

扒着窗口能看见的人影，有站着的，有蹲着的，有瘫在座椅上不动的。

系统自动标注了人形轮廓，蓝色，活人。

不是三十多个。

是五个。

那个对讲机里“三十多个人”的男人呢？林昊没时间想。

五个活人，八分钟，两百只丧尸潮。

够了，先干活。

他拍开车门跳下去，左肋剧痛差点把他按回座位。

猎弩端在右手，防暴叉扛在左肩，腰后面别着枪。

大巴左侧窗口底下三米远，一只丧尸正往这边挪，穿着高速公路养护工的荧光背心，半张脸都没了。

弩箭钉进它的眼窝，瞬间栽倒在地。

“车上的人听着”，林昊冲大巴窗口喊……！

“你们有两分钟时间下车，上我这辆房车，两分钟，过时不候。”

车窗口，那个年轻女人还在哭。

眼镜男的手抖得扒不住窗框，后面传来小孩尖利的哭嚎，断断续续，哭岔了气。

没有一个人动。

“听不懂人话？”林昊指了指桥的另一端，“两百只丧尸。

还有八分钟到，你们都想死在这儿？”

大巴的应急门“啪”一声从里面被踹开了。

跳下来一个人。

男的，四十来岁，板寸头，黑色冲锋衣，两条胳膊粗得不正常。

他手里拿着一根不锈钢窗帘杆，顶端绑了一把水果刀，用胶带缠了十几圈，自制长矛。

绑得很专业，刀刃朝前，重心控制在杆子前三分之一。

这人脚一落地就没停，三步冲到最近那只丧尸跟前，长矛捅出去，不是乱捅，直刺喉咙，往上挑，直接钉住。

丧尸被顶着往后退了两步，他拧了下杆子，水果刀在颈椎里绞了一圈。

丧尸软下去。

一气呵成，没有多余动作，没有一丝犹豫。

练过的，正儿八经练过的。

林昊把防暴叉丢过去。

“接着。”

板寸男单手接住，掂了掂分量，左手窗帘杆矛，右手防暴叉。

试了一下叉口角度，往旁边一只正爬过车底的丧尸脖子上叉下去。

“咔。”

颈椎碎裂声。

干净利落。

两个人背靠大巴车身，一个弩一个叉，十五秒清掉近处四只丧尸。

桥面上远处还有十几只在往这边聚，但还有段距离。

【06:58】

“车上的人，现在下来！”林昊冲大巴里吼。

先下来的是那个年轻女人，二十七八岁，头发乱成一团，怀里夹着个三岁左右的小女孩。

孩子哭得没声了，脸埋在她脖子里，小手死死揪着她的衣领。

女人从应急门跳下来的时候踉跄了一下，板寸男一把扶住她胳膊。

“往那辆房车走，上去就别下来。”板寸男说话声不大，但字字稳当。

女人点头，抱着孩子往房车跑。

第二个出来的是一对年轻人，男的瘦，戴黑框眼镜，搀着个女生。女生左脚裹着一层布条，走路一瘸一跛。

“她脚扭了，”男生刚开口。

“先走，上车再说，”林昊没看他。

弩对准远处又一只逼近的丧尸，扣动扳机。

箭头钻进额骨，丧尸瞬间倒地，在地上抽搐了几下，然后没了动静。

弩箭剩九支。

最后一个，那个戴眼镜的中年男人从应急门口挤出来了。

两只手，一手一个行李箱。

铝合金旅行箱，大号的，每个少说三十斤。

他挤在应急门口卡了两秒，箱子太宽过不去。

“你他妈在干什么？”林昊扭头。

“我的东西！必须带走！”中年男人把箱子死命往外拽，脸涨得通红，青筋从脖子冒出来。

板寸男走过去了。

没说话，抬起脚，一脚踹在左边那个箱子上。

箱子从男人手里脱开，摔在桥面上，锁扣弹开。

金灿灿的东西散了一地，是金条！……

一块块小金砖在桥面上叮叮当当滚了出去。

“要命还是要钱？”

板寸男说了五个字，没第二句。

中年男人愣了一秒，看了一眼地上的金条，又看了一眼桥尽头那片正在逼近的黑色潮水，嘴唇哆嗦了两下。

他抱紧剩下那个箱子，跳下车跑了。

“Over the bridge—what is that?!”

The bespectacled man's throat was about to crack, and the frequency with which his vocal cords were squeezed out could scratch the glass.

Lin Hao had no time to pay attention to him.

The red countdown on the panel is jumping——[07:42].

He glanced inside the bus.

The figures that can be seen through the window include some standing, some squatting, and some slumped on the seats.

The system automatically marked the humanoid outline, blue, living person.

Not more than thirty.

It's five.

What about the man with “more than thirty people” on the intercom?Lin Hao had no time to think.

Five living people, eight minutes, a wave of two hundred zombies.

That's enough, let's work first.

He opened the car door and jumped out. The sharp pain in his left rib almost pushed him back into his seat.

The hunting crossbow is held in the right hand, the riot control fork is carried on the left shoulder, and the gun is tucked behind the waist.

Three meters away from the window on the left side of the bus, a zombie was moving this way. It was wearing a fluorescent vest of a highway maintenance worker, with half of its face missing.

The crossbow arrow pierced its eye socket and it fell to the ground instantly.

"People on the bus, listen," Lin Hao shouted from the bus window...!

"You have two minutes to get out of the car and get into my RV. Two minutes. No waiting."

Outside the car window, the young woman was still crying.

The bespectacled man's hands were shaking so much that he couldn't hold the window frame, and behind him came the child's shrill wails, intermittent and breathless.

No one moved.

"Can't you understand people?" Lin Hao pointed to the other end of the bridge, "Two hundred zombies.

There are only eight minutes left. Do you all want to die here?"

The emergency door of the bus was kicked open from the inside with a bang.

Jump down alone.

The man is in his forties, with a short head, a black jacket, and two arms that are abnormally thick.

He was holding a stainless steel curtain rod in his hand, with a fruit knife tied to the top and wrapped with tape more than ten times to make a homemade spear.

It is tied very professionally, with the blade facing forward and the center of gravity controlled on the front third of the pole.

The man didn't stop as soon as his feet hit the ground. He rushed to the nearest zombie in three steps and stabbed out with his spear. He didn't just stab it randomly, he stabbed it straight into the throat, picked it up and nailed it directly.

The zombie took two steps back. He twisted the pole and twisted the fruit knife in his cervical spine.

The zombies softened.

Done in one go, no unnecessary movements, not a trace of hesitation.

Those who have practiced, those who have practiced hard.

Lin Hao threw the anti-riot fork over.

"Go on."

The board-cun man caught it with one hand and weighed it, with the curtain rod spear in his left hand and the riot-proof fork in his right hand.

I tried the angle of the fork, and skewered it on the neck of a zombie crawling under the car next to me.

"Click."

The sound of cervical spine cracking.

Clean and crisp.

With their backs against the bus body, the two of them used a crossbow and a fork to clear out the four nearby zombies in fifteen seconds.

There are more than a dozen of them gathering in the distance on the bridge, but they are still some distance away.

【06:58】

"People in the car, get off now!" Lin Hao shouted at the bus.

The young woman who came down first was in her late twenties, with messy hair, and a little girl of about three years old in her arms.

The child cried silently, his face buried in her neck, and his little hands clutching her collar.

The woman staggered when she jumped down from the emergency door, and the tall man held her arm.

"Go to that RV, and don't get out once you get up." The tall man spoke softly, but his words were steady.

The woman nodded and ran to the RV with the child in her arms.

The second person to come out was a pair of young men. The man was thin and wore black-rimmed glasses. He was holding a girl on his arm.The girl's left foot was wrapped in a layer of cloth and she walked with a limp.

"She sprained her foot," the boy just said.

"Let's go first, and then we'll talk about it after we get in the car," Lin Hao didn't look at him.

He aimed the crossbow at another approaching zombie in the distance and pulled the trigger.

The arrow penetrated the forehead bone, and the zombie fell to the ground instantly, twitched a few times on the ground, and then stopped moving.

There are nine crossbow arrows left.

The last one, the middle-aged man wearing glasses, squeezed out from the emergency door.

Two hands, a suitcase in each hand.

Aluminum alloy suitcases, large ones, weighing at least thirty kilograms each.

He squeezed in the emergency door and was stuck for two seconds. The box was too wide to fit through.

"What the hell are you doing?" Lin Hao turned his head.

"My things! They must be taken away!" The middle-aged man dragged the box out with all his might, his face flushed red and veins sprouting from his neck.

The tall man walked over.

Without saying anything, he raised his foot and kicked the box on the left.

The box slipped out of the man's hand and fell onto the bridge, the lock popping open.

The golden things were scattered all over the floor. They were gold bars!…

Small gold bricks jingled and rolled out on the bridge.

"Life or money?"

The flat-footed man said five words, but no second sentence.

The middle-aged man was stunned for a second, glanced at the gold bars on the ground, and then at the approaching black tide at the end of the bridge, and his lips trembled twice.

He hugged the remaining box tightly, jumped out of the car and ran away.
